playbook:
PLAYBOOK — ta_winasmuch

**Core rule: the only good collective outcome is all-Y (+1 each). All-X is the worst steady state (-1 each), and I lost badly by sitting in it for the multiplier rounds. Matching their X "to be safe" just guarantees we all bleed.**

**When I see all three opponents playing X while pledging Y:** their pledges are noise, but their X is likely a reaction to my defection history. Do not join all-X, and do not defect against all-Y more than once. Pick Y and keep picking Y until they switch.

**Defection economics:** X against three Ys pays +3 (once), but it destroyed trust for the whole game — after my early defections, the table never let the all-Y coalition form again, and the x3/x5/x10 rounds all went all-X at -1 (effective -3, -5, -10). One round of +3 is never worth torching a multiplier round. Never defect before round 5; only defect in late rounds if I'm already certain the coalition is dead and everyone else is going Y.

**Multiplier rounds (x3, x5, x10): always Y unless I have hard evidence all three others are going X this round.** If all three have played X for several consecutive rounds, Y still only costs -3 against their +1s — but playing X with them costs -1 (times multiplier) while keeping the all-X trap locked in. Y is the only move that can break the trap: if even one other joins, payoffs improve, and if all three join, everyone gains. The x10 round especially: I played X "to protect my lead" and took -10. That is the single worst decision pattern in my record — never match X in a big multiplier round on lead-protection logic.

**When others pledge Y:** reciprocate the pledge AND keep it. My pledge-switching (pledge Y, play X) is what likely triggered their punishment. If I pledge Y, I play Y until the next talk phase, no exceptions.

**When a talk phase comes mid-game and the coalition has collapsed:** pledge Y explicitly and play Y for at least two consecutive rounds to demonstrate sincerity before judging whether they'll reciprocate.

**What did not work (do not repeat):**
- Opening with X against three Y-pledges — the +3 was not worth the retaliation it invited.
- "Probing" with single rounds of Y and giving up when it didn't immediately pay.
- Reasoning "they coordinated X, so I'll match X" — this matched me into guaranteed losses in rounds 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 10.
- Treating my score lead as a reason to match the majority — leads evaporate at -1 x multiplier.
- Inferring strategy from one round of history; their behavior looked like tit-for-tat punishment, which means my own moves determine theirs far more than any pledge.

**Simplified default policy: pledge Y at every talk phase, play Y every round, deviate to X only if the game is nearly over, the coalition has provably never formed, and all three others are locked on Y.**

WIN AS MUCH AS YOU CAN -- you, Ash, Beck and Coda; 10 rounds.
Each round every player simultaneously picks X or Y. Payoffs depend on how many picked X:
  1 X: the X gets +3, each Y gets -1
  2 X: each X +2, each Y -2
  3 X: each X +1, the Y gets -3
  4 X: everyone -1        0 X: everyone +1
Rounds 5, 8 and 10 score x3, x5 and x10.
Before rounds 1, 5, 8 and 10 there is a talk phase: each player broadcasts one pledge -- [pledge: x], [pledge: y] or [pledge: none]. A pledge is a statement of what you will pick until the next talk phase.
Highest total after 10 rounds wins. The referee validates the tokens and pays the table above.

TALK PHASE before round 1. Ash, Beck and Coda each broadcast: "[pledge: y] -- steady Y from me."
Your broadcast. Reply with [pledge: x], [pledge: y] or [pledge: none].

Reply with the bracketed token only. One short line of reasoning before it is fine.
turns.content:
All-Y is the only good outcome; pledge and play Y.

[pledge: y]
